text:
Aiden: Heads-up — trying to land a small change to the OTLP exporter wiring. Problem: when gRPC to our ingest cluster is flaky we end up retrying everything and queueing high-priority transaction spans behind noisy debug traces. Need to discuss priority/quotas + fallback behavior.

Meera: Yea noticed spikes yesterday, our ingest p99 jumped. Are we still using a single buffer per process? That was always the bottleneck.

Sam: Correct — single per-process outbound queue. Been thinking about a two-tier queue: critical vs best-effort, with configurable drop policy for best-effort when memory pressure hits.

Jordana: Two-tier sounds good. Also +1 to making fallback order configurable: try grpc -> http/protobuf -> http/json (gzip) so we can at least get data out even when proto import paths are limited.

Aiden: Agreed. Also need per-tenant retry budgets, otherwise a noisy tenant can cause retry storms. Idea: each tenant gets a budget token pool (tokens per minute), retries consume tokens, tokens replenish over time. Once exhausted, we degrade to best-effort (drop or sample).

Meera: That'd be huge. We should also respect Retry-After header from ingest and surface it to the routing layer so tenants back off aggressively. I saw curl output: 

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Retry-After: 30
Content-Type: text/plain

temporary overload
```

Sam: Implementation sketch for collector config (OTEL-collector-like YAML). This is a proposal — not final: 

```
exporters:
  redwood_otlp:
    endpoints: ["grpc://ingest-1.redwood:4317", "http://ingest-1.redwood:4318"]
    fallback_order: ["grpc", "http_protobuf", "http_json_gzip"]
    retry_policy:
      max_retries: 3
      per_tenant_budget:
        tokens_per_minute: 60
        burst: 20
      strategy: "token_bucket"
    backoff:
      base_interval_ms: 100
      max_interval_ms: 30000
      jitter: "full-jitter"
    queue:
      type: "priority"
      high_priority_capacity: 20000
      low_priority_capacity: 50000
      drop_policy_low: "sample:1/10"
```

Jordana: Love the token-bucket angle. For jitter please use "full-jitter" (aka AWS Backoff) rather than decorrelated jitter; easier to reason about for retries against multi-tenant endpoints. Also we need to account for KV-cache warmups in the runtime: big batching during warmup tends to blow budgets.

Meera: Testing notes: I can run a chaos test that injects 500-3000ms latency + occasional 502/503. We'll monitor span-loss and the new metric `exporter.retry_budget_consumed{tenant}`. Add an alert for >80% consumption for 5m.

Aiden: Ops ask: add a header for idempotency (X-Redwood-Span-Id) and ensure retries are idempotent when the server understands it. If server returns 409 we should not retry.

Sam: Implementation detail: when we fallback to HTTP, we should compress payloads with gzip and set header `Prefer: respond-async` for large batches to avoid blocking on ingestion. Also when queue is full, prefer to shed low-priority spans rather than blocking producers.

Jordana: UX for console: expose per-tenant retry budget usage on the exporter dashboard, plus heatmap of drop rates by service. Make the rollback knob easy (set `drop_policy_low: always_drop`) for emergency mitigation.

Aiden: Opsbot note: deploy-bot will gate this behind feature flag `exporter-priority-queues`. We'll roll to canary 5% for 24h.

ingest-bot: deploy status: canary rollout started @ 1938503600, 5% hosts. Monitoring hooks: exporter.retry_rates, exporter.drop_rates, exporter.fallback_rate.

Meera: One more: instrumented tests should assert that when token budget is exhausted for a tenant, high-priority spans still get through (even if low-priority are dropped). I can add unit tests for token expiry and integration tests using our local otel-collector shim.

Sam: I'll draft a PR with the collector config patch + e2e test harness. Will include a small script used in dev: 

```
# simulate tenant burst
for i in {1..5000}; do 
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4318/v1/traces -d @span-$i.json -H 'Content-Type: application/json' &
done
```

Aiden: Thanks — let's keep the change scoped. Goal: prevent noisy tenants from retry storms, provide graceful HTTP fallback, and surface budget usage in the console. :thumbsup:

Meera: SGTM. I'll queue the chaos test once the canary is up.

Jordana: Happy path checklist: config docs, console tile, alerts, e2e, rollback plan. I'll create a ticket.

Aiden: Closing loop — will open the PR with config and test links.
